title: dan — and
explanation: dan joins two things, two describing words or two whole sentences, just like English and: sayur dan buah (vegetables and fruit), besar dan bersih (big and clean), Saya kerja di bank dan istri saya guru. In a list it goes before the last item only: kopi, teh, dan air putih. The one thing dan can't mean is with: for being or going with someone, Indonesian uses dengan (Saya pergi dengan teman), and in everyday speech sama (Saya pergi sama teman).
natural: Lists, pairs of describing words and two related facts, in any register. Between two short sentences people often just pause instead: Saya guru, istri saya dokter.
stiff: Don't use dan to string actions together in order (I got up and showered and left): for one thing after another, lalu or terus sounds natural. And Saya pergi dan teman doesn't mean I went with a friend; say dengan teman, or sama teman.

examples.indonesian: Kemarin saya beli sayur dan buah di pasar.
examples.english: Yesterday I bought vegetables and fruit at the market.

gap.why: You bought both, so dan joins them, as and does in English.

combine.a: Kemarin saya beli sayur di pasar.

examples.english: The room is big and clean.

gap.why: Two good things side by side take dan; tapi would need a contrast, as in besar tapi kotor.

examples.indonesian: Saya kerja di bank dan istri saya guru.
examples.english: I work at a bank, and my wife's a teacher.

gap.why: Two whole sentences join with dan; dengan only means with.

examples.indonesian: Besok saya mau ke pantai dengan teman-teman.
examples.english: Tomorrow I'm going to the beach with some friends.

gap.note: sama means with here too, and it's what most people say in everyday speech.
gap.why: Going together with someone is dengan; dan only joins two equal things, as in saya dan teman saya.
